title: jscpd gate is a permanent false positive: `"format": "console"` makes jscpd analyze zero files
body:
## Summary

`.jscpd.json` in this template sets `"format": "console"`. In jscpd, `format` is the list of **languages/formats to analyze**, not the output format — output is controlled by `reporters` (which this file already sets correctly).

Because `console` is not a source language, jscpd matches **zero files** and always reports `Found 0 clones.` The duplication gate is therefore a permanent false positive: it can never fail, no matter how much duplicated code a repository contains.

Found while working on [link-foundation/start#158](https://github.com/link-foundation/start/issues/158) ("check for all false positives, false negatives, warnings and errors in CI/CD").

## Reproducible example

Two deliberately identical files plus this template's `format` setting:

```bash
mkdir jscpd-repro && cd jscpd-repro
printf 'function a(){\n  const x=1;\n  const y=2;\n  const z=3;\n  return x+y+z;\n}\n' > a.js
printf 'function b(){\n  const x=1;\n  const y=2;\n  const z=3;\n  return x+y+z;\n}\n' > b.js
printf '{"threshold":0,"minTokens":10,"minLines":3,"format":"console","reporters":["console"]}' > .jscpd.json

npx --yes jscpd .
```

Actual output:

```
Found 0 clones.
```

Exit code `0` — the gate passes despite 100 % duplication between the two files.

Remove `"format": "console"` (or set it to real languages) and re-run:

```bash
npx --yes jscpd . --format javascript
```

```
Found 1 clones.
ERROR: jscpd found too many duplicates (41.7%) over threshold (0.0%)
```

This is not theoretical for real repositories either: in a repository using this template's config verbatim, `npx jscpd .` reports "No duplicates found", while `npx jscpd . --format "javascript"` on the same tree reports 24 files / 49 clones / **5.64 %** duplication.

## Workaround

Override on the command line until the config is fixed:

```bash
npx jscpd . --format "javascript,typescript,jsx,tsx,markdown"
```

## Suggested fix

Drop the `format` key so jscpd uses its default language set, or list the languages the repository actually contains. `reporters` already carries the console output, so nothing is lost:

```diff
   "ignore": [
     ...
   ],
-  "format": "console",
   "reporters": ["console", "html"],
   "output": "./reports/jscpd"
 }
```

or, to be explicit:

```diff
-  "format": "console",
+  "format": ["javascript", "jsx", "typescript", "tsx", "json", "markdown", "yaml"],
```

Note that fixing this will make the gate start reporting real duplication, so repositories adopting the fix may need to set a non-zero `threshold` (or extend `ignore`) in the same change rather than being surprised by a suddenly red pipeline.

## Suggested regression test

Since the failure mode is silent, a check that jscpd actually analyzed something is worth adding to the workflow — e.g. assert the JSON reporter's `statistics.total.sources > 0`, so a future config typo fails loudly instead of turning the gate green.

title: fix(ci): expose timeout cancellations as failures
body:
## What

- Add a terminal `pipeline-status` job that runs with `if: always()` and observes every other job in `release.yml`.
- Fail that gate for any failed job and for cancelled jobs on `main`; keep non-default-ref cancellations as warnings.
- Preserve in-progress `main` checks while retaining superseded-run cancellation on other refs.
- Add a patch changeset and regression coverage that prevents the gate dependency list from drifting.

## Why

GitHub Actions reports jobs killed by `timeout-minutes` as `cancelled`, not `failure`. Without an aggregate observer, a timed-out release job can leave the whole run grey and hide a broken release pipeline.

## Reproduction

A workflow job with `timeout-minutes: 1` that runs `sleep 300` concludes `cancelled`. Before this change, `release.yml` had no terminal job that translated that conclusion into a visible failure.

## Testing

- `npm test` — 212 passed after merging the latest `main`
- `npm run check` — lint, Prettier, and duplication checks passed
- GitHub Actions runtime matrix — Node, Bun, and Deno passed on Ubuntu, macOS, and Windows
- GitHub Actions security — CodeQL and dependency review passed
- `bash scripts/check-file-line-limits.sh`
- `bash -n scripts/check-pipeline-status.sh`
- `GITHUB_BASE_REF=main node scripts/validate-changeset.mjs`

Fixes #123

title: ci: add CodeQL and dependency review

title: release.yml: a job killed by timeout-minutes is reported as 'cancelled', so timeouts silently pass CI
body:
## Summary

A job killed by its own `timeout-minutes` is reported by GitHub Actions as **`cancelled`**, not **`failure`**. A workflow run whose only non-success job is cancelled inherits the run conclusion `cancelled` too — which on the runs list is visually indistinguishable from "a human pressed cancel" or "a newer push superseded this run". It is grey, not red. It does not appear in the failed-runs filter and it sends no failure notification.

`release.yml` in this template has no job that observes the aggregate result, so a timing-out job produces a silently-green-looking pipeline.

This is not hypothetical. In [link-assistant/formal-ai](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai), which is derived from this template, **18 consecutive `CI/CD Pipeline` runs on `main` concluded `cancelled` over three days** while `Auto Release` was timing out. Nobody triaged them, because nothing looked broken. The damage: **11 versions (0.326.2 … 0.333.0) were published to crates.io and tagged in git with no GitHub Release at all**, because `Create GitHub Release` sits after the Docker publish step and was never reached.

## Reproducible example

```yaml
name: repro
on: workflow_dispatch
jobs:
  slow:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 1
    steps:
      - run: sleep 300   # killed at 1m
  other:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: echo ok
```

Dispatch it. The `slow` job is killed and annotated *"The job has exceeded the maximum execution time of 1m0s"* — and both the job and the **whole run** conclude `cancelled`. `gh run list` shows no failure. Add `if: failure()` to any step and observe that it does not fire.

## Workaround

Set every job's `timeout-minutes` well above the tool's own internal timeout (e.g. Playwright's `globalTimeout`, `pytest-timeout`, `cargo nextest --slow-timeout`) so the *tool* aborts first, exits non-zero, and the job reports `failure`. This only helps for jobs that have such a tool.

## Suggested fix

Add a terminal gate job that `needs:` every other job and runs `if: always()`. The key nuance — and the reason an off-the-shelf action like [`re-actors/alls-green`](https://github.com/re-actors/alls-green) is not quite right here — is that a cancellation must be treated **differently on the default branch**. `release.yml` already sets

```yaml
concurrency:
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}
```

so `main` is never superseded, and a cancelled job there can **only** be a timeout or a deliberate manual cancel. On other refs, a cancellation is the ordinary superseded-run case and must stay a warning, or every force-push would go red.

```yaml
  pipeline-status:
    name: Pipeline Status
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    if: always()
    needs: [ ...every other job... ]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - name: Fail the run when a required job was cancelled or failed
        env:
          NEEDS_JSON: ${{ toJSON(needs) }}
          IS_MAIN: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name == 'push' }}
        run: bash scripts/check-pipeline-status.sh
```

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
: "${NEEDS_JSON:?NEEDS_JSON is required (pass toJSON(needs))}"
IS_MAIN="${IS_MAIN:-false}"

select_by_result() {
  printf '%s' "$NEEDS_JSON" \
    | jq -r --arg want "$1" \
        'to_entries | map(select(.value.result == $want) | .key) | join(", ")'
}

failed="$(select_by_result failure)"
cancelled="$(select_by_result cancelled)"

echo "Failed jobs:    ${failed:-<none>}"
echo "Cancelled jobs: ${cancelled:-<none>}"

status=0
if [ -n "$failed" ]; then
  echo "::error::Pipeline failed. Failing jobs: ${failed}"
  status=1
fi
if [ -n "$cancelled" ]; then
  if [ "$IS_MAIN" = "true" ]; then
    echo "::error::Pipeline has cancelled jobs on main: ${cancelled}. A job killed by 'timeout-minutes' is reported as cancelled, which would otherwise hide the failure."
    status=1
  else
    echo "::warning::Cancelled jobs: ${cancelled}. On a non-default ref this is usually a superseded run."
  fi
fi
exit "$status"
```

Two details worth keeping:

- **`needs:` must list every job.** Any job left out can still time out unobserved. A test that diffs the job list against the gate's `needs:` catches drift — that is exactly how I found a missing job in my own implementation.
- **Always print both lists before deciding.** The next grey run then explains itself in its own log instead of requiring a 25 000-line log download.

The implementation, a behavioural test over all four conclusion states, and the full incident reconstruction are in link-assistant/formal-ai#977 / [PR #978](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/978).

title: Add CI security scanning: CodeQL (code + GitHub Actions workflows) and dependency-review
body:
The pipeline has thorough lint / test / coverage / release automation, but **no security analysis at all**: there is no CodeQL workflow, no `actions/dependency-review-action`, no SBOM step, and no vulnerability scanner anywhere under `.github/`.

## Reproduction

Against `main` (verified 2026-08-05):

```bash
gh api repos/link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/git/trees/HEAD?recursive=1 \
  --jq '.tree[].path' | grep -iE 'codeql|dependabot|security'
# -> no output

grep -rniE 'codeql|dependency-review|security-events|sbom|trivy|grype|osv-scanner|npm audit' .github/
# -> no matches
```

So a pull request that adds a vulnerable dependency, or a workflow change that
leaks `GITHUB_TOKEN` into an injectable `run:` block, merges with every check
green. This template is copied into new repositories as the CI baseline, so the
blind spot is inherited by every downstream project.

Note that CodeQL also analyses **GitHub Actions workflows** themselves
(`language: actions`), which is directly relevant here: this repository is
mostly workflow code, and past issues in this repo were exactly of that class
(for example expression interpolation into `run:` bodies and a missing
top-level `permissions:` block).

## Workaround

Until the workflow lands, each downstream repository can enable
*Settings → Code security → Code scanning → CodeQL → Default setup* by hand,
and run ``npm audit --audit-level=high`` locally. Both are per-repository manual steps that a
template is supposed to remove.

## Suggested fix

Add `.github/workflows/security.yml`:

```yaml
name: Security

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 6 * * 1'

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  codeql:
    name: CodeQL (${{ matrix.language }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    concurrency:
      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-codeql-${{ matrix.language }}
      cancel-in-progress: true
    permissions:
      contents: read
      security-events: write
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        language: [javascript-typescript, actions]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - uses: github/codeql-action/init@v3
        with:
          language: ${{ matrix.language }}
      - uses: github/codeql-action/autobuild@v3
      - uses: github/codeql-action/analyze@v3

  dependency-review:
    name: Dependency Review
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - uses: actions/dependency-review-action@v4
        with:
          fail-on-severity: high
          comment-summary-in-pr: on-failure
```

Both are free on public repositories. Keeping this in a separate workflow file
(rather than inside `release.yml`) matches the existing separation of
`docs.yml` / `links.yml` and keeps `release.yml` from growing further.

## Cross-template status

Verified absent in **all four** pipeline templates on 2026-08-05, so this is a
fleet-wide gap rather than a single-template omission:

| Template | HEAD checked | CodeQL / dependency-review / SBOM / scanner |
|---|---|---|
| `js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template` | `7b70923` | none |
| `rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template` | `c867f78` | none |
| `python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template` | `98d6dca` | none |
| `csharp-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template` | `6806bd9` | none |

## Provenance

Found by a four-template CI/CD comparison audit run in downstream
`link-assistant/formal-ai` (report:
<https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-479/template-comparison/REPORT.md>,
finding 6 / upstream recommendation 1; filed under
<https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/894>). The downstream repo
has the same gap and is fixing it locally as well.

title: fix(ci): gate manual releases on quality checks
body:
Fixes #119

## Problem

The manual `instant-release` and `changeset-pr` jobs had no dependencies, so they could begin writing to `main` before validation finished. In particular, an instant release could publish a broken package even when lint or tests failed later in the same workflow run.

There was a second dependency-path concern: `detect-changes` is skipped for `workflow_dispatch`, so simply adding `needs: [lint, test]` would leave the manual jobs permanently skipped unless the quality-gate conditions explicitly survive that skipped dependency.

## Solution

- Run `lint` for manual dispatches while preserving cancellation propagation.
- Run the test matrix for `instant` manual dispatches.
- Make `instant-release` depend on `lint` and `test`, and require both results to be `success`.
- Make `changeset-pr` depend on the faster `lint` gate and require a successful result.
- Keep `!cancelled()` in each condition so skipped transitive dependencies remain evaluable without allowing cancelled runs to write.
- Add a patch changeset.

## Reproduction and regression coverage

Before the workflow change, the new `manual release quality gates` tests fail because the writer jobs have no `needs`, lint/tests do not run on manual dispatch, and cancellation/result checks are absent.

The regression tests now evaluate the workflow conditions and verify that:

- successful lint and tests allow an instant release;
- either lint or test failure blocks publishing;
- changeset PR creation waits for successful lint;
- cancellation blocks both manual writer jobs.

## Testing

- `npm test` — 203 passed
- `bun test --timeout 30000` — 203 passed
- `deno test --allow-read` — 172 passed
- `npm run check` — lint, Prettier, and duplication checks passed
- `bash scripts/check-mjs-syntax.sh` — passed
- `bash scripts/check-file-line-limits.sh` — passed
- `node scripts/validate-changeset.mjs` with PR refs — passed
- Ruby YAML parser validation for `.github/workflows/release.yml` — passed

title: sanitize-npm-userconfig.mjs leaves the setup-node placeholder _authToken, breaking OIDC trusted publishing
body:
`scripts/sanitize-npm-userconfig.mjs` removes the deprecated `always-auth` key but
keeps the `_authToken` line that `actions/setup-node` writes. When a project has no
`NPM_TOKEN` secret and relies on OIDC trusted publishing, that leftover line makes
npm believe it is already authenticated, so it never performs the OIDC exchange and
the registry rejects the anonymous upload with a misleading `E404`.

**Reproduction**

1. Generate a project from this template; do not set an `NPM_TOKEN` secret.
2. Configure a trusted publisher for the package on npmjs.com.
3. Trigger the release workflow.

The publish step fails with:

```
npm error code E404
npm error 404 Not Found - PUT https://registry.npmjs.org/<package>
```

and every step of the job shows `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX` in its
environment, even though the workflow sets no token. The npm user config at
`$NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG` contains
`//registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken=${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}`.

**Root cause**

`actions/setup-node` with `registry-url` unconditionally writes that line and
exports the placeholder — see actions/setup-node#1440 and #1551. The fix
(actions/setup-node#1558) shipped only on the v7 line; `@v6` still contains the
placeholder in `dist/setup/index.js`.

**Workaround**

Strip the line after `setup-node` and before `npm publish`:

```bash
sed -i '/_authToken/d' "$NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG"
```

**Suggested fix in code**

Extend `sanitize-npm-userconfig.mjs` to remove the `_authToken` line as well,
unless a real credential is present. A token is "real" only when it is non-empty
and is neither `XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX` nor an unexpanded `${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}`:

```js
const AUTH_TOKEN_LINE = /^[^\S\r\n]*(?:\/\/[^\s=]*:)?_authToken[^\S\r\n]*=.*(?:\r?\n|$)/gim;

export function sanitizeNpmrc(content, { keepAuthToken = false } = {}) {
  const withoutAuthToken = keepAuthToken ? content : content.replace(AUTH_TOKEN_LINE, '');
  return withoutAuthToken.replace(ALWAYS_AUTH_LINE, '');
}
```

It is also worth failing fast with actionable guidance when neither a usable token
nor OIDC request variables (`ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL` /
`ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN`) are available, so the failure names the missing
configuration instead of surfacing a bare `E404`. Moving the template to
`actions/setup-node@v7` fixes the root cause too, but the sanitiser change is
version-agnostic and protects projects that are still pinned to `@v6`.

A working implementation, with tests, is in
`js/scripts/prepare-npm-auth.mjs` of link-foundation/meta-language (PR #192).

title: Manual release jobs have no `needs:`, so an instant release publishes to npm without lint or tests
body:
## Summary

In `.github/workflows/release.yml`, both manual-dispatch jobs are declared with **no `needs:` at all**:

```yaml
  instant-release:
    name: Instant Release
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.event.inputs.release_mode == 'instant'
```

```yaml
  changeset-pr:
    name: Create Changeset PR
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.event.inputs.release_mode == 'changeset-pr'
```

(lines 527-529 and 646-648 at the current `main`.)

Because a job with no `needs:` starts immediately and in parallel with every other job, `instant-release` runs its full publish sequence — version bump, commit to `main`, `npm publish` via OIDC trusted publishing, GitHub release — while `lint` and `test` are still running, or even after they have failed. The workflow run is then marked failed, but the package is already on the registry and the version commit is already on `main`. npm does not allow republishing that version, so recovery means a deprecate/unpublish plus another bump.

This contradicts the pipeline's own best-practice #9 ("validated releases only"), which every other release path in the template does follow: the automatic `release` job is correctly gated on `needs: [lint, test]`.

## Reproduction

1. Generate a repository from this template.
2. Introduce a deliberate failure, e.g. add `const x =;` to a source file, or make a unit test assert `false`.
3. Push it to `main`.
4. Run the workflow manually: **Actions -> Release -> Run workflow**, with `release_mode: instant` and `bump_type: patch`.

Observed: `lint` and `test` go red, and `instant-release` publishes the broken code to npm anyway.
Expected: `instant-release` never starts once a quality gate has failed.

## Workaround

Only trigger `release_mode: instant` from a commit whose CI is already green, and check the run of that exact SHA first. This is a policy, not a control — nothing in the workflow enforces it.

## Suggested fix

Add the dependency and gate on the dependency *results*, not merely on job completion. `needs:` alone is not sufficient here: `detect-changes` is skipped on `workflow_dispatch`, and a skipped dependency skips its dependents unless the condition survives it (see [actions/runner#491](https://github.com/actions/runner/issues/491)). `!cancelled()` keeps the condition evaluable while still stopping the job when the run is cancelled.

```yaml
  instant-release:
    name: Instant Release
    needs: [lint, test]
    if: >-
      !cancelled() &&
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      github.event.inputs.release_mode == 'instant' &&
      needs.lint.result == 'success' &&
      needs.test.result == 'success'
```

```yaml
  changeset-pr:
    name: Create Changeset PR
    needs: [lint]
    # A changeset PR does not publish, so it only waits on the fast lint gate.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() &&
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      github.event.inputs.release_mode == 'changeset-pr' &&
      needs.lint.result == 'success'
```

Note the block scalar: `if: !cancelled() && ...` written on a single line is invalid YAML, because a plain scalar may not begin with `!` (the tag indicator).

## Context

Found while auditing CI/CD false positives and false negatives in a repository seeded from this template: link-foundation/browser-commander#75. The fix above is applied there in link-foundation/browser-commander#76.

title: fix(ci): reject unsupported workflow concurrency keys
body:
## What

- Scan every checked-in workflow concurrency block and fail tests when a key other than `group` or `cancel-in-progress` is present.
- Add a minimal `queue: max` regression fixture proving the policy detects the reported invalid key.
- Document GitHub Actions' supported concurrency keys and pending-job behavior.
- Add a patch changeset for the generated-workflow safeguard.

## Why

GitHub Actions concurrency blocks support only `group` and `cancel-in-progress`; `queue: max` causes actionlint v1.7.12 to report an unexpected key. The invalid key was not present in current `main` or the prepared branch when this fix began, so this change closes the regression gap that allowed an exact expected block to pass even if an unsupported sibling key was added later. Existing `cancel-in-progress: false` writer behavior is preserved.

## Reproduction

The focused regression fixture contains:

```yaml
concurrency:
  group: main-writer
  cancel-in-progress: false
  queue: max
```

The new policy scanner reports `queue` as unsupported. It also scans every `.yml` and `.yaml` file in `.github/workflows`.

## Verification

- `actionlint` v1.7.12 over `.github/workflows/*.yml`

- `deno test --allow-read` — 167 passing

title: Remove unsupported queue key from workflow concurrency blocks
body:
The generated workflow adds `queue: max` to write-job concurrency blocks. GitHub Actions concurrency supports only `group` and `cancel-in-progress`, so actionlint v1.7.12 reports:

```text
unexpected key "queue" for "concurrency" section. expected one of "cancel-in-progress", "group"
```

Reproduction:

```bash
actionlint .github/workflows/*.yml
```

Please remove `queue: max` from all job concurrency sections and update tests/docs that require it. `cancel-in-progress: false` already preserves the running write; GitHub manages at most one pending run per concurrency group.

title: fix(ci): harden workflow inputs and writer concurrency
body:
## What

- Route pull-request branch names and manual release inputs through step environment variables before shell use.
- Add a workflow-wide regression scan that rejects contributor-controlled expressions in every `run:` block.
- Configure `init.defaultBranch=main` before checkout in all workflows.
- Move concurrency from workflow scope to job scope: stale read-only jobs cancel independently, while Pages, preview generation, npm releases, Docker publishing, and changeset PR creation share one non-cancelling writer queue.
- Default the example-app workflow token to read-only and escalate permissions only on deploy/write jobs.
- Document cancellation, dependency, active-writer, and matrix edge cases.
- Add a patch changeset.

## Why

GitHub expands expressions before the shell parses a `run:` command. A fork branch name or free-form workflow-dispatch description could therefore become executable shell syntax. Workflow-level cancellation also cannot save CI minutes on read-only `main` checks without risking interruption of an already-running publisher.

## Reproduction

Before the workflow changes, the new focused tests failed because:

1. `changeset-check` interpolated `github.head_ref` directly into Bash.
2. Both manual release paths interpolated free-form dispatch values directly into commands.
3. `example-app.yml` and `links.yml` lacked checkout-time default-branch configuration.
4. Workflows used run-level concurrency, and several write/deploy jobs lacked the shared protected writer group.

## Verification

- `npm test` — 196 passing
- `bun test --timeout 30000` — 196 passing
- `deno test --allow-read` — 165 passing
- `npm run check`
- `bash scripts/check-mjs-syntax.sh`
- `bash scripts/check-file-line-limits.sh`
- `GITHUB_BASE_REF=main node scripts/validate-changeset.mjs`
- Parsed all workflow YAML files successfully

title: release.yml interpolates github.head_ref and workflow_dispatch inputs into run: scripts; two workflows miss the init.defaultBranch env
body:
Found while auditing a downstream repository against this template (link-assistant/agent#287). Two of the template's own rules are not applied to `release.yml` itself.

## 1. `${{ github.head_ref }}` is interpolated into a shell script (injection)

`.github/workflows/release.yml` (changeset-check job):

```yaml
        env:
          GITHUB_BASE_REF: ${{ github.base_ref }}
          ...
        run: |
          if [[ "${{ github.head_ref }}" == "changeset-release/"* ]]; then
```

`github.head_ref` is the head branch name of a pull request, which for a fork PR is chosen by the contributor. Expressions are substituted into the script text *before* bash runs, so a branch named e.g. `a"$(id>/tmp/x)"b` executes as code in the `pull_request` job. The step already passes `github.base_ref` through `env:`; `head_ref` should be handled the same way:

```yaml
        env:
          HEAD_REF: ${{ github.head_ref }}
        run: |
          if [[ "$HEAD_REF" == "changeset-release/"* ]]; then
```

## 2. `github.event.inputs.description` is interpolated into `run:` (injection)

`.github/workflows/release.yml`:

```yaml
        run: node scripts/version-and-commit.mjs --mode instant --bump-type "${{ github.event.inputs.bump_type }}" --description "${{ github.event.inputs.description }}"
```

and the same pattern in the changeset-pr job for `create-manual-changeset.mjs`. `description` is `type: string`, i.e. free-form, and these jobs hold the publishing permissions. `bump_type` is a `choice` so it is constrained, but `description` is not. Passing both through `env:` and reading them in the scripts keeps them as data.

## 3. The default-branch env is missing from two of the three workflows

`release.yml` sets

```yaml
env:
  GIT_CONFIG_COUNT: '1'
  GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0: init.defaultBranch
  GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0: main
```

but `example-app.yml` and `links.yml` do not, so every job in them logs `hint: Using 'master' as the name for the initial branch` from the `git init` that `actions/checkout` runs.

## Suggested guard

These are all mechanically checkable, in the spirit of `tests/workflow-permissions.test.js`. The downstream repository added a rule that scans every `run:` block of every workflow for `/\$\{\{\s*(?:inputs\.|github\.event\.inputs\.|github\.head_ref)[^}]*\}\}/` and a rule that requires `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0: init.defaultBranch` in every workflow.

title: simulate-fresh-merge.sh: unquoted $BASE_REF on lines 40 and 50 can silently skip the merge-conflict check
body:
`scripts/simulate-fresh-merge.sh` expands `$BASE_REF` unquoted on two lines, while quoting it correctly everywhere else in the same file. Both unquoted expansions are on the paths that decide whether the fresh-merge simulation runs at all, so a base branch name containing whitespace or a glob character turns a merge-conflict detector into a silent pass.

## Evidence

Current `main` (verified against the API, not a local copy):

```sh
$ grep -n '\$BASE_REF' scripts/simulate-fresh-merge.sh
19:echo "=== Synchronizing PR with latest $BASE_REF ==="
28:echo "Fetching latest $BASE_REF..."
29:git fetch origin "$BASE_REF"      # quoted
33:BASE_SHA=$(git rev-parse "origin/$BASE_REF")   # quoted
36:echo "Latest base branch ($BASE_REF): $BASE_SHA"
40:BEHIND_COUNT=$(git rev-list --count HEAD..origin/$BASE_REF)   # UNQUOTED
43:  echo "Merge preview is up-to-date with $BASE_REF. No simulation needed."
50:  if git merge origin/$BASE_REF --no-edit; then                # UNQUOTED
```

Lines 29 and 33 quote it; lines 40 and 50 do not. The file is internally inconsistent, which is what makes this look like an oversight rather than a deliberate choice.

`shellcheck` flags both as SC2086:

```
In scripts/simulate-fresh-merge.sh line 40:
BEHIND_COUNT=$(git rev-list --count HEAD..origin/$BASE_REF)
                                                 ^-------^ SC2086: Double quote to prevent globbing and word splitting.

In scripts/simulate-fresh-merge.sh line 50:
  if git merge origin/$BASE_REF --no-edit; then
                      ^-------^ SC2086: Double quote to prevent globbing and word splitting.
```

## Reproduction

Git allows spaces in branch names (`git check-ref-format` rejects only a specific character set; space is not in it, though `refs/heads/a b` is legal only via `--branch` rules — the glob case below needs no unusual naming at all).

Minimal, no unusual repo required — the glob path:

```sh
git init -q repo && cd repo
git commit -q --allow-empty -m base
git branch 'release-1.x'        # a real, ordinary branch name
git checkout -q -b feature
git commit -q --allow-empty -m work
# a file in the working tree whose name matches the branch pattern:
touch 'origin/release-1.x'      # any path that the glob can expand to
```

More directly, with `BASE_REF` carrying an unexpected value:

```sh
$ BASE_REF='main -- .' bash -c 'git rev-list --count HEAD..origin/$BASE_REF'
```

The unquoted expansion splits into three words, so `git rev-list` receives arguments the script never intended. In the workflow, `BASE_REF` comes from `${{ github.base_ref }}`, which is attacker-influenced on pull requests from forks only insofar as the *branch name* is chosen by the PR author's base selection — but the failure mode does not need hostility. It needs one word-splitting character.

**Why it matters even in the benign case:** when line 40 mis-parses, `BEHIND_COUNT` is empty or wrong, and `[ "$BEHIND_COUNT" -eq 0 ]` on line 42 either errors under `set -e` or takes the "up-to-date, no simulation needed" branch. That branch is the *skip* branch: the fresh-merge check reports success while never having merged anything. A conflict that the script exists to catch reaches `main`.

## Workaround

Consumers of the template can quote the two expansions in their own copy:

```diff
-BEHIND_COUNT=$(git rev-list --count HEAD..origin/$BASE_REF)
+BEHIND_COUNT=$(git rev-list --count "HEAD..origin/$BASE_REF")
```

```diff
-  if git merge origin/$BASE_REF --no-edit; then
+  if git merge "origin/$BASE_REF" --no-edit; then
```

## Suggested fix

Apply the two-line diff above. Two further hardening steps, both already present in the sibling Rust template's version of this script, are worth considering in the same change:

1. Add `shellcheck` to the lint job so SC2086 cannot reappear. The Rust template's copy is clean under `shellcheck --severity=warning`; this one is not.
2. Replace the `rev-list --count` ancestry test with `git merge-base --is-ancestor "origin/$BASE_REF" HEAD`, which short-circuits without arithmetic on a string that may be empty — removing the class of failure rather than the instance.

## Context

Found while auditing a downstream repository's pipeline against all three `*-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template` repos: link-assistant/formal-ai#812. The downstream copy was adopted from this template verbatim and inherited both unquoted expansions; it has been fixed there, with the divergence from upstream noted in the file header so the next sync does not silently revert it.

The Rust template's `scripts/simulate-fresh-merge.sh` does not have this defect — it quotes every expansion. The Python template does not ship the script at all (tracked separately as link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#35).

title: fix(publish): poll npm registry for verification instead of republishing
body:
Fixes #105

## Problem

`scripts/publish-to-npm.mjs` treated "publish succeeded" and "verification succeeded" as one retryable unit. When the publish worked but the single check 2s later missed because npm's registry had not propagated, the retry loop re-ran the whole `changeset publish`, which then failed with "cannot publish over the previously published versions" — turning a successful release into a reported failure.

## Solution

New module `scripts/publish-retry.mjs` splits the two failure domains:

- `waitForVersionOnRegistry()` — bounded polling with exponential backoff (7 attempts, 2s → 30s cap). A thrown E404/network error is treated as a miss and polling continues.
- `publishWithRetry()` — retries `changeset publish` **only** when the publish command itself failed. Once a publish reports success, the flow moves to verification and never re-enters the publish path; an exhausted poll fails the release without republishing.
- `isAlreadyPublishedError()` — `EPUBLISHCONFLICT` / "cannot publish over the previously published versions" is treated as a cue to verify, not to fail.

Verification is still mandatory: a publish that falsely claims success still fails the release.

`publish-to-npm.mjs` now delegates to `publishWithRetry`; `attemptPublish` became `runPublishCommand` (publish only, no verification). Non-retryable auth guidance from #77 is preserved.

## Reproduction / tests

`tests/publish-retry.test.js` encodes the scenario from the issue — a runner whose publish succeeds once and whose verification misses twice:

- one publish, verification eventually succeeds, success ✅ (previously: a second publish attempt and a conflict)
- exhausted verification polling fails without republishing
- publish-command failures still retry
- non-retryable auth errors still fail fast
- backoff sequence is capped at `maxDelay`

All 169 tests pass; `npm run lint`, `format:check` and `check:duplication` are clean.

title: ci: build Dockerfile on pull requests so a broken image fails the PR
body:
Fixes #106

## Problem

`docker-publish` (`.github/workflows/release.yml`) is gated on `needs: [release, instant-release]` with `published == 'true'`, so the image is only ever built **after** the package is published. A Dockerfile regression cannot fail a pull request; it produces a half-finished release (package published, no image).

## Solution

New `docker-build` job that runs on pull requests with code changes, before any release job:

- `push: false` + `load: true` — works for fork pull requests, which have no registry credentials (`DOCKERHUB_TOKEN` is never referenced by this job).
- `cache-from/cache-to: type=gha` — shares the buildx layer cache with the publish build.
- `timeout-minutes: 30`, matching `docker-publish`.
- Reuses the existing `./.github/actions/setup-buildx-resilient` action.

Because this template ships no Dockerfile by default, `scripts/check-docker-build.mjs` gates the build steps: no Dockerfile → the job succeeds as a no-op; Dockerfile present (path overridable via `vars.DOCKERFILE` / `vars.DOCKER_CONTEXT`, same variables the publish path uses) → the image is built. A missing build context is a hard error.

## Tests

`tests/docker-build.test.js` (new, 6 cases):
- the workflow job exists, needs `detect-changes`, is PR-gated, and has a timeout;
- it builds with `push: false` / `load: true` / GHA cache and never references `DOCKERHUB_TOKEN`;
- it is not gated on the release jobs (the regression this issue reports);
- config evaluation: disabled with no Dockerfile (no error), enabled with one, error on a missing context.

`tests/ci-timeouts.test.js` updated with the new job's expected timeout.

Full suite: 162 tests passing across the node/bun/deno matrix locally; eslint + prettier clean. A changeset is included.

title: CI: Dockerfile is only built after publish, so a broken image cannot fail a pull request
body:
Found while auditing a downstream consumer of the Rust sibling of this template (`link-assistant/formal-ai`, issue [#808](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/808)). This template is the best of the three on every other axis — it is the only one with `simulate-fresh-merge.sh`, `secretlint`, and clean `!cancelled()` guards — but it shares one gap.

## The Dockerfile is never built at pull-request stage

`docker-publish` (`.github/workflows/release.yml:552`) is gated on the release jobs:

```yaml
  docker-publish:
    name: Optional Docker Hub Publish
    needs: [release, instant-release]
    if: |
      !cancelled() &&
      (
        (needs.release.result == 'success' && needs.release.outputs.published == 'true') ||
        (needs.instant-release.result == 'success' && needs.instant-release.outputs.published == 'true')
      )
```

So the image is only ever built *after* the package has been published. A Dockerfile regression cannot fail a pull request; it produces a half-finished release instead — package published, no image, no image-bearing GitHub Release. We hit exactly that downstream (runs 29312084458 and 29485000765).

**Suggested fix** — a build-only pull-request job. `push: false, load: true` keeps it working for fork pull requests, which have no registry credentials, and the GHA layer cache keeps the common case off a cold build:

```yaml
  docker-build:
    name: Docker Image Build Check
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    needs: [detect-changes]
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && needs.detect-changes.outputs.any-code-changed == 'true'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v4
      - uses: docker/build-push-action@v7
        with:
          context: .
          push: false
          load: true
          tags: app:pr-check
          cache-from: type=gha
          cache-to: type=gha,mode=max
```

If the repo also ships a runtime-contract script baked into the image, run it here too (`docker run --rm app:pr-check <verifier>`) — that is what we did downstream, where the verifier existed but had no caller anywhere in CI.

**Workaround** without a new job: add `docker build .` to an existing pull-request job, at the cost of not sharing the buildx layer cache with the publish build.

Companion reports for the siblings, which have additional gaps this template does not: link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#100, link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#35.

Happy to open a pull request for this if useful.

release.yml has no top-level permissions: block, so jobs inherit the default GITHUB_TOKEN scope
body:
## Summary

`.github/workflows/release.yml` has **no top-level `permissions:` block**. The file goes straight from `on:` to `concurrency:`, so every job inherits the repository's default `GITHUB_TOKEN` scope — which on many organisations is still read/write-all.

This matters more here than in an ordinary workflow: `release.yml` is the file that publishes packages, pushes tags and commits, and creates releases, so it is the highest-value token in the repository.

## Reproducible check

```bash
gh api repos/OWNER/REPO/contents/.github/workflows/release.yml --jq .content \
  | base64 -d | grep -n '^permissions:' || echo "NONE"
# -> NONE
```

Then compare against the effective grant:

```bash
gh api repos/OWNER/REPO/actions/permissions/workflow --jq .default_workflow_permissions
# -> "write" on organisations that have not changed the default
```

Any workflow step — or any compromised third-party action, all of which float on mutable major tags here — then runs with write access to repository contents.

## Suggested fix

Add least-privilege at the top of the file and escalate per job only where needed:

```diff
 on:
   push:
     branches: [main]

+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
 concurrency:
```

Then, on the jobs that genuinely need more:

```yaml
  release:
    permissions:
      contents: write      # create tags/releases
      id-token: write      # trusted publishing / attestations
```

`link-assistant/formal-ai` applies exactly this pattern (`release.yml:32-33`, with per-job escalation) and its release pipeline works unchanged.

## Workaround

Organisation owners can set **Settings → Actions → Workflow permissions → Read repository contents** as the default, but that is repo-external configuration that a template consumer will not inherit when they generate a new project from this template. The fix belongs in the template so every generated repository is safe by default.

## Scope

Filed against all three pipeline templates (`rust-`, `js-`, `python-`); verified missing in each. Discovered while auditing CI/CD against these templates in link-assistant/formal-ai#796.

title: Suppress Git default-branch checkout warning in release workflow
body:
The release workflow uses `actions/checkout@v6` but does not set Git's default initial branch before checkout runs. On GitHub-hosted runners with Git 2.54, checkout initializes the repository before any user-defined step can run and emits this warning:

```text
hint: Using 'master' as the name for the initial branch. This default branch name
hint: will change to "main" in Git 3.0. To configure the initial branch name
hint: to use in all of your new repositories, which will suppress this warning,
hint: call:
hint:
hint:  git config --global init.defaultBranch <name>
```

Observed example: https://github.com/link-foundation/gh-pull-all/actions/runs/28363495995

Related downstream fix: https://github.com/link-foundation/gh-pull-all/pull/47

## Reproduction

1. Run any workflow job in this template that starts with `actions/checkout@v6` on a runner where Git emits the Git 3.0 default-branch hint.
2. Inspect the checkout log. The warning appears during checkout's internal `git init`, before a normal workflow step could run `git config --global init.defaultBranch main`.

Local reproduction of the workaround:

```bash
git init /tmp/git-default-branch-warning

GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 \
GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=init.defaultBranch \
GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=main \
git init /tmp/git-default-branch-configured
```

The configured command initializes the repository without the default-branch hint.

## Workaround

Set Git runtime config at workflow scope so it is present for `actions/checkout` itself, not only for later shell steps:

```yaml
env:
  GIT_CONFIG_COUNT: '1'
  GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0: init.defaultBranch
  GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0: main
```

## Suggested Fix

title: Harden generated preview-image pushes against non-fast-forward races
body:
The JS template's example-app workflow has the same direct generated-push pattern that failed in link-assistant/calculator issue 195.

Reproducible example:
1. A push to main starts a workflow that regenerates preview/screenshot artifacts.
2. While that job is running, another main-writing workflow commits first, such as an automated release/version bump.
3. The preview job commits generated files and runs plain `git push origin HEAD:main`.
4. Git rejects the push with `main -> main (fetch first)` / `failed to push some refs` because the remote branch advanced.

Concrete evidence from calculator:
- https://github.com/link-assistant/calculator/actions/runs/28194099705 failed in Update Screenshots with a non-fast-forward push rejection.
- The failure happened while the release pipeline from the same merge was also writing to main.

Template location:
- `.github/workflows/example-app.yml` commits preview images with `git push origin HEAD:main` and no rebase/retry path.

Suggested fix:
- Put jobs that write generated files to main behind a shared main-writer concurrency group.
- Replace plain pushes with a helper that does `git push origin HEAD:main`, and on rejection runs `git pull --rebase origin main` before retrying.
- Add a small local regression test using a bare Git remote and two clones to prove the helper handles a non-fast-forward race.

Workaround until fixed:
- Manually rerun the failed generated-artifact workflow after the release/version-bump workflow finishes, or rebase the generated commit locally and push it again.

title: Detect real merge pushes with first-parent diff
body:
Found while investigating link-assistant/web-capture#139.

## Problem

`scripts/detect-code-changes.mjs` treats any merge commit as a GitHub
`pull_request` synthetic merge and compares `HEAD^2^..HEAD^2`.

That is correct for pull request runs when the workflow wants the PR head's
latest-commit diff. It is wrong for a real merge commit pushed to `main`.

If a branch has:

1. an earlier commit that changes JavaScript code, and
2. a final commit that only changes docs,

then the merge commit pushed to `main` is diffed as only the final docs commit.
The detector reports code flags such as `mjs-changed`, `js-changed`, and
`any-code-changed` as `false`, even though the merge introduced code.

## Reproducer

1. Create `main` with an initial commit.
2. Create a `feature` branch.
3. Commit a source change, for example `src/index.mjs`.
4. Commit a docs-only change, for example `docs/notes.md`.
5. Merge the branch to `main` with `git merge --no-ff feature`.
6. Run `GITHUB_EVENT_NAME=push node scripts/detect-code-changes.mjs`.

Expected: the push merge detects the full merge diff and reports code changed.

Actual: the script compares `HEAD^2^..HEAD^2`, sees only the docs-only final
feature commit, and reports no code change.

## Suggested fix

Only use the `HEAD^2^..HEAD^2` pull-request behavior when
`GITHUB_EVENT_NAME == 'pull_request'`. For push merge commits, compare the first
parent to the merge commit, for example `git diff --name-only HEAD^1 HEAD`.

The Python and C# templates already branch on `GITHUB_EVENT_NAME`; this JS
template should do the same.

title: extractReleaseNotes regex lacks end-anchor: '1.2' matches the '1.2.3' section
body:
## Summary

`extractReleaseNotes()` builds the version-header regex without an **end anchor** after the version, so extracting notes for `1.2` can match the section that actually belongs to `1.2.3` (a prefix match).

## Location

`scripts/create-github-release.mjs:95-96`

```js
const versionHeaderRegex = new RegExp(
  `## ${escapeRegex(version)}[\\s\\S]*?(?=## \\d|$)`
);
```

The `escapeRegex()` call (added to neutralize the `.` wildcard) is correct, but `## 1\.2` still matches at the start of a `## 1.2.3` header because nothing requires the version token to end.

## Reproduction

CHANGELOG:

```md
## 1.2.3
- newer notes

## 1.2
- older notes
```

`extractReleaseNotes(changelog, '1.2')` returns the **1.2.3** notes (it matches starting at `## 1.2.3`), publishing the wrong section for the `1.2` release.

## Suggested fix

Anchor the end of the version token:

```js
const versionHeaderRegex = new RegExp(
  `## ${escapeRegex(version)}(?=\\s|$)[\\s\\S]*?(?=## \\d|$)`
);
```

(The Rust template's `create-github-release.rs` is immune — it uses `(?m)^## \[{escaped}\]`, bracket-delimited and line-anchored.)

## Notes

Found while auditing the downstream `link-assistant/web-search` release pipeline (issue #17). The same unanchored pattern exists there and is being fixed; the Python/C# templates that derive their changelog extraction from this script likely share it.

title: Support multi-language monorepos: auto-detect layout, namespace release tags/titles, badge the artifact
body:
## Support multi-language monorepos: auto-detect layout, namespace releases, and badge the artifact

When a repository hosts more than one language (e.g. `js/` + `rust/` in one monorepo, each driven by its template's release workflow), the per-language releases collide in a single flat namespace and the GitHub release does not link to the artifact it published. Discovered while shipping [link-assistant/web-search#15](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-search/issues/15); full write-up in [PR #16](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-search/pull/16) (`docs/case-studies/issue-15`).

### Request

Make the release job adapt with **no configuration**:

1. **Auto-detect layout.** Manifest at the repo root → single-language; manifest in a language subdirectory (`js/package.json`, `js/package.json`, `rust/Cargo.toml`, …) → multi-language.
   ```bash
   if [ -f package.json ]; then ROOT=.; MULTI=false; else ROOT=js; MULTI=true; fi
   ```
2. **Namespace the tag** in multi-language mode: `js_v<version>` (keep a plain `v<version>` single-language).
3. **Prefix the release title** `[JavaScript] <version>` in multi-language mode (`<name> <version>` single-language).
4. **Badge the published artifact** in the release body — a shields.io badge linking to the exact version page: `https://www.npmjs.com/package/<pkg>/v/<version>`. Build the link from the **bare** version (strip any `v`/`lang_v` prefix first) so it resolves to the version page rather than 404ing.

A small, unit-tested helper keeps tag/title construction **idempotent** (re-running on an already-prefixed version must not double-prefix).

### Reference implementation

`js/scripts/release-naming.mjs` (+ `release-naming.test.js`, 21 cases) and the `version` step of `.github/workflows/rust.yml` in [link-assistant/web-search#16](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-search/pull/16).

title: Release pipeline lacks an install-from-package smoke test (indexing check is not enough)
body:
## Summary

The `release.yml` pipeline publishes to npm and waits for the version to be
indexed (`verifyPublished`), but it never **installs the published package from
npm into a clean project and runs it**. There is no install-from-package smoke
test, so a successfully-published-but-broken package (bad `files`, wrong `bin`
path, misconfigured `exports`) still produces a green release.

## Reproducible example

1. Misconfigure packaging (e.g. drop the CLI entry from `files`, or point `bin`
   at a path that is not packaged).
2. Push a release. `changeset publish` succeeds and `npm view <pkg>@<ver>`
   resolves, so the release is green.
3. A consumer runs `npm install <pkg>@<ver>` and `npx <bin>` — and it fails.

## Why indexing checks are not enough

The release pipeline already polls the registry until the new version is
*indexed* (e.g. `Wait for crate/NuGet indexing`, `verifyPublished`). That proves
the version *exists*, not that it is *usable*. A package can index perfectly yet
be broken for consumers when:

- `files` / `package.include` / packaged paths omit a required file
- the `bin` / `[[bin]]` / entry-point path is wrong or not executable
- `main` / `exports` / the published module shape is misconfigured
- a runtime dependency is declared as a dev-dependency (so it is missing on install)

In every one of these cases the release goes green and the release notes
advertise an install command that does not work.

## Suggested fix

Add a **post-publish smoke-test step** that installs the just-published artifact
from the registry into a throwaway project (NOT the repo checkout) and exercises
each advertised entry point (library import, CLI, and HTTP server if any),
with retries to absorb registry-propagation lag. Fail the release loudly if any
entry point is broken.

## Reference implementation

`link-assistant/web-search` (issue
[#6](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-search/issues/6)) implements exactly
this:

- npm: [`js/scripts/smoke-test-package.mjs`](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-search/blob/main/js/scripts/smoke-test-package.mjs)
  — temp project, `npm install <pkg>@<version>` with retries, then verifies
  library import + `--list-providers` CLI + `serve` HTTP `/health`.
- crates.io: an inline `Smoke-test published crate` step in
  [`.github/workflows/rust.yml`](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-search/blob/main/.github/workflows/rust.yml)
  — `cargo install <crate>@<version>`, run the binary, and compile a fresh
  dependent crate against the library.

Happy to open a PR porting the pattern back to this template.

title: CI: `test` job runs the full suite on non-code changes (skipped changelog/changeset-check is treated as 'run tests')
body:
## Summary

The `test` job in `.github/workflows/release.yml` runs the full test matrix on **changes that touch no code at all** (docs-only commits, `.gitkeep` edits, changeset-only commits). This wastes CI minutes and slows iteration.

## Root cause

```yaml
test:
  needs: [detect-changes, changeset-check, test-compilation, lint, check-file-line-limits]
  if: |
    !cancelled() &&
    (github.event_name == 'push' || needs.changeset-check.result == 'success' || needs.changeset-check.result == 'skipped') &&
    (needs.test-compilation.result == 'success' || needs.test-compilation.result == 'skipped') &&
    (needs.lint.result == 'success' || needs.lint.result == 'skipped') &&
    (needs.check-file-line-limits.result == 'success' || needs.check-file-line-limits.result == 'skipped')
```

On a non-code change, **every** upstream job is *skipped* (they all gate on `detect-changes`), so each clause matches its `== 'skipped'` branch and the whole condition is satisfied — `test` runs even though nothing relevant changed. The condition has **no positive "did code change?" gate**; it only checks that upstream jobs did not *fail*. `skipped` means "no code changed at all," which is exactly when tests should NOT run.

## Reproducible example

1. Open a PR whose only change deletes a line from `.gitkeep` (or edits a `*.md` file).
2. `test-compilation`, `lint`, `check-file-line-limits`, `changeset-check` all **skip**, yet **`test` still runs**.

Confirmed downstream in `link-assistant/formal-ai#442` (a sibling pipeline) where the analogous defect ran the full suite for a one-line `.gitkeep` deletion.

## Suggested fix

Add an explicit change-detector gate (keep the existing fast-check `== 'skipped'` guards — those are legitimate). The **python template** is the correct reference: gate on the `detect-changes` outputs.

```yaml
test:
  if: |
    !cancelled() &&
    (
      github.event_name == 'push' ||
      needs.detect-changes.outputs.any-code-changed == 'true' ||
      needs.detect-changes.outputs.mjs-changed == 'true' ||
      needs.detect-changes.outputs.js-changed == 'true' ||
      needs.detect-changes.outputs.package-changed == 'true' ||
      needs.detect-changes.outputs.workflow-changed == 'true'
    ) &&
    (github.event_name == 'push' || needs.changeset-check.result == 'success' || needs.changeset-check.result == 'skipped') &&
    (needs.test-compilation.result == 'success' || needs.test-compilation.result == 'skipped') &&
    (needs.lint.result == 'success' || needs.lint.result == 'skipped') &&
    (needs.check-file-line-limits.result == 'success' || needs.check-file-line-limits.result == 'skipped')
```

## General principle

Gate jobs on **change-detector outputs**, never *solely* on whether sibling jobs were skipped. `skipped` is ambiguous (it can mean "irrelevant change" or "nothing changed") and inverts easily. rust/csharp/js templates share this defect; the python template is the correct reference.

_Reported from the downstream fix in link-assistant/formal-ai#442 / link-assistant/formal-ai#443._

`401`/`403`/`ENEEDAUTH`/`Access token expired` are **permanent** — retrying
wastes ~28s and hides the real cause behind a generic
`❌ Failed to publish after 3 attempts`.

**Fix:** A new `scripts/publish-failure-classifier.mjs` exposes
`isNonRetryableFailure()` and `buildAuthFailureGuidance()`. When a publish error
matches a non-retryable pattern, `attemptPublish()` flags it and the retry loop
**fails fast** with an actionable message explaining the first-publish
bootstrap, instead of retrying.

### Problem 2 — No first-publish bootstrap path (OIDC cannot create a new package)

npm trusted publishing requires a *trusted publisher* configured on npmjs.com,
which can only be done for a package that **already exists**. The first publish
of a brand-new package therefore cannot use OIDC and fails with `E404`.

**Fix:** Both `Publish to npm` steps (the `release` and `instant-release` jobs)
now pass an optional `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}`. When
`NPM_TOKEN` is set, the first publish succeeds; once the package exists and a
trusted publisher is configured, OIDC takes over and the token can be removed.
Documented in `README.md`.

## How to reproduce the original issue

Run the release workflow for a scoped package that has never been published and
without a configured trusted publisher / token — npm returns `E404` and the old
script retried 3× before failing with a generic message.

## Tests

- `tests/publish-failure-classifier.test.js` — asserts E404/401/403/auth output
  is classified non-retryable, transient errors stay retryable, matching is
  case-insensitive and null-safe, and the guidance names the package +
  `NPM_TOKEN`/`NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`.
- `tests/workflow-reliability.test.js` — asserts both publish steps pass
  `secrets.NPM_TOKEN` as `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`.

All 84 tests pass locally (`npm test`); lint, format, and duplication checks are

title: publish-to-npm.mjs retries permanent failures and there is no first-publish bootstrap path
body:
# Upstream report: `publish-to-npm.mjs` retries permanent failures and there is no first-publish bootstrap path

Target repository: `link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template`

Discovered while fixing `link-assistant/web-search#11`. Two related problems in
the npm release path cause a brand-new package's **first release to fail** and
make the failure slow and hard to diagnose.

---

## Problem 1 — Permanent failures are retried `MAX_RETRIES` times and surfaced as a generic error

### Where

`scripts/publish-to-npm.mjs`

```js
const FAILURE_PATTERNS = [
  'packages failed to publish',
  'error occurred while publishing',
  'npm error code E',
  'npm error 404',
  'npm error 401',
  'npm error 403',
  'Access token expired',
  'ENEEDAUTH',
];
// ...
for (let i = 1; i <= MAX_RETRIES; i++) {
  console.log(`Publish attempt ${i} of ${MAX_RETRIES}...`);
  const { success, error } = await attemptPublish(/* ... */);
  if (success) { /* ... */ return; }
  if (i < MAX_RETRIES) {
    console.log(`Publish failed: ${error.message}, waiting ${RETRY_DELAY / 1000}s before retry...`);
    await sleep(RETRY_DELAY);
  }
}
console.error(`❌ Failed to publish after ${MAX_RETRIES} attempts`);
process.exit(1);
```

Every detected failure is treated as retryable. But `npm error 404` (first
publish of a package that does not exist yet) and `401`/`403`/`ENEEDAUTH`/
`Access token expired` are **permanent** — retrying cannot help.

### Reproducible example

Run the release workflow for a scoped package that has never been published and
without a configured trusted publisher / token. Observed (from
`link-assistant/web-search` run 27448599744):

```
npm error code E404
npm error 404 Not Found - PUT https://registry.npmjs.org/@scope%2fpkg - Not found
The requested resource '@scope/pkg@0.8.1' could not be found or you do not have permission to access it.
...
Publish attempt 1 of 3...
Publish attempt 2 of 3...
Publish attempt 3 of 3...
❌ Failed to publish after 3 attempts
```

~28 seconds are wasted on retries, and the final message hides the real cause.

### Workaround

Set a real `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` (see Problem 2) so the first publish succeeds; this
sidesteps the retry path but does not fix the misclassification.

### Suggested fix

Classify non-retryable patterns and exit immediately with actionable guidance:

```js
const NON_RETRYABLE_PATTERNS = [
  'npm error 404', 'npm error 401', 'npm error 403',
  'e404', 'e401', 'e403',
  'access token expired', 'eneedauth',
  'you must be logged in', 'unable to authenticate',
];

function isNonRetryableFailure(output) {
  const lower = output.toLowerCase();
  return NON_RETRYABLE_PATTERNS.some((p) => lower.includes(p));
}
```

In the retry loop, when `error?.nonRetryable` is set, print guidance that
explains the first-publish bootstrap and exit `1` without retrying. Reference
implementation: `js/scripts/publish-to-npm.mjs` in
`link-assistant/web-search` PR #12.

---

## Problem 2 — No first-publish bootstrap path (OIDC cannot create a new package)

### Where

`.github/workflows/release.yml` — the `Publish to npm` steps run
`node scripts/publish-to-npm.mjs` with `id-token: write` but **no**
`NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`. They rely solely on npm OIDC trusted publishing.

### Why it fails

npm trusted publishing requires a *trusted publisher* to be configured on
npmjs.com, which can only be done for a package that **already exists**. The
first publish of a brand-new package therefore cannot use OIDC and fails with
E404 (see Problem 1). The template's documented "just push and it releases"
flow is broken for the very first release of any new package.

### Suggested fix

Add an optional token bootstrap fallback on the publish steps:

```yaml
- name: Publish to npm
  id: publish
  env:
    NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
  run: node scripts/publish-to-npm.mjs --should-pull
```

When `NPM_TOKEN` is set, the first publish succeeds; once the package exists and
a trusted publisher is configured, OIDC takes over and the token can be removed.
This keeps OIDC as the steady-state mechanism while unblocking bootstrap.
Document that `NPM_TOKEN` is only needed for the first release.

title: ci: resilient buildx boot with mirror fallback for publish-dockerhub
body:
## Summary

`publish-dockerhub` booted buildx with `docker/setup-buildx-action@v4` and no pinned-image pre-pull. The default `docker-container` driver pulls `moby/buildkit:buildx-stable-1` straight from Docker Hub at boot, so a transient `registry-1.docker.io` outage failed the whole publish job — even with nothing wrong in the code or build.

This ports the resilient buildx boot pattern from `link-foundation/box` (issues #97 / #100) into this template.

## Changes

- **New composite action** `.github/actions/setup-buildx-resilient/action.yml`:
  1. Pre-pulls the pinned BuildKit image from canonical Docker Hub with retries + exponential backoff.
  2. On a full registry outage, falls back to `mirror.gcr.io` (Google's pull-through cache on independent infrastructure) and re-tags it to the canonical reference.
  3. Boots buildx with `driver-opts: image=…` pinned so the driver reuses the locally cached image and never touches the failing registry.
  4. Non-fatal fall-through if both sources are down (preserves prior worst-case behaviour).
- **`publish-dockerhub/action.yml`** now calls `setup-buildx-resilient` instead of `docker/setup-buildx-action@v4`.
- **`docs/case-studies/issue-75/CASE-STUDY.md`** documenting symptom, root cause, and fix.
- **Changeset** for a patch release.

## How to reproduce the original failure

Block `registry-1.docker.io` on a runner (hosts/iptables blackhole) and run the buildx step — the boot pull fails at *"Creating a new builder instance"*.

## Tests

- `tests/setup-buildx-resilient.test.js` extracts the real pre-pull `run:` block from the action and drives it with a mock `docker`, asserting recovery for: healthy registry (no mirror touched), registry-down/mirror-up (recovers + re-tags), and both-down (non-fatal warning). Runs in CI via `npm test`.
- `experiments/test-issue75-buildx-mirror-fallback.sh` is the standalone offline reproduction of the same scenarios.

title: CI: buildx boot in publish-dockerhub pulls moby/buildkit from Docker Hub with no mirror fallback — transient registry outage fails publishing
body:
## Summary

The `publish-dockerhub` composite action boots buildx with `docker/setup-buildx-action@v4` (then `docker/build-push-action@v7`) and no pinned-image pre-pull. The default `docker-container` driver makes dockerd pull `moby/buildkit:buildx-stable-1` from Docker Hub at boot. When `registry-1.docker.io` has a transient outage, that boot pull fails and takes the whole publish job down — even though nothing is wrong with the code or the build.

This is the same class of failure investigated downstream in `link-foundation/box` issue #100 (a ~2.5-minute Docker Hub registry outage failed the buildx boot) and originally issue #97.

## Reproduction

Any release run where `registry-1.docker.io` is unreachable for longer than a normal blip will fail at **Set up Docker Buildx → Creating a new builder instance** with:

```
ERROR: Error response from daemon: Get "https://registry-1.docker.io/v2/": net/http: request canceled while waiting for connection (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)
```

You can simulate it by blocking `registry-1.docker.io` (e.g. a hosts/iptables blackhole) on a runner and then running the buildx step.

## Workaround

Re-run the job once Docker Hub recovers.

## Suggested fix

Pre-pull the pinned BuildKit image before booting, with a retry loop **and a pull-through registry-mirror fallback** (`mirror.gcr.io`, on independent infrastructure), then re-tag it to the canonical reference so the boot reuses the local copy and never touches the failing registry. `link-foundation/box` implements this as a reusable composite action `setup-buildx-resilient`:

- Action: `.github/actions/setup-buildx-resilient/action.yml`
- Case study: `docs/case-studies/issue-100/CASE-STUDY.md`

Minimal sketch:

```yaml
- name: Pre-pull BuildKit image (retry + mirror fallback)
  shell: bash
  run: |
    img=moby/buildkit:buildx-stable-1
    pull() { for d in 5 10 20 40 0; do docker pull "$1" && return 0; sleep "$d"; done; return 1; }
    pull "$img" && exit 0
    pull "mirror.gcr.io/$img" && { docker tag "mirror.gcr.io/$img" "$img"; exit 0; }
    echo "::warning::could not pre-pull $img; letting buildx try its own boot pull"
- name: Set up Docker Buildx
  uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v4
  with:
    driver-opts: image=moby/buildkit:buildx-stable-1
```

Happy to port the full resilient action over if useful.

title: ci: add concurrency block to links.yml
body:
## Summary

`.github/workflows/links.yml` (Broken Link Checker) was the only workflow in this template missing a `concurrency:` block. Because it triggers on `push` (main) and `pull_request` like its siblings, pushing multiple commits in quick succession left redundant link-check runs in flight instead of cancelling superseded ones — wasting CI minutes.

This adds the same `concurrency` block already used by `release.yml` and `example-app.yml`, placed immediately after the `on:` section:

```yaml
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}
```

The `github.ref != 'refs/heads/main'` guard keeps the main-branch run from being cancelled mid-flight while still cancelling redundant PR/branch runs — consistent with the rest of the template.

- `.github/workflows/links.yml` — added the `concurrency` block (with explanatory comment matching the sibling workflows).

title: preview-regen: guard Playwright Chromium install with timeout+retry and cache (CDN can stall with no internal timeout)
body:
## Summary

The `preview-regen` job in `.github/workflows/example-app.yml` installs the
Playwright Chromium browser with no per-step timeout, no retry, and no browser
cache. The Playwright CDN (`cdn.playwright.dev`) can stall a download after the
bytes finish transferring, with **no internal timeout**, hanging the step until
the job-level `timeout-minutes` fires. This wastes a full runner-timeout window
(~20 min) on every transient stall and re-downloads the ~170 MiB browser on
every run.

## Where

`.github/workflows/example-app.yml`, job `preview-regen`:

```yaml
- name: Install browser automation dependencies
  env:
    PLAYWRIGHT_SKIP_BROWSER_DOWNLOAD: '1'   # good: postinstall download skipped
  run: npm install --no-save --package-lock=false --no-audit --no-fund browser-commander@0.8.1 playwright@1.59.1

- name: Install Chromium for preview rendering
  run: npx playwright install --with-deps chromium   # <-- no timeout, no retry, no cache
```

The `PLAYWRIGHT_SKIP_BROWSER_DOWNLOAD: '1'` guard on the npm install is correct,
but the subsequent explicit `npx playwright install` is unguarded.

## Impact observed downstream

We hit this exact stall in `link-assistant/hive-mind` (a near-identical
preview-regen + e2e Pages workflow modelled on this template): the Chromium
download reached 100% of 170.4 MiB, then the connection stalled on the next
asset with no timeout and the job hung for ~22 minutes before the runner
cancelled it.

## Suggested fix

Two complementary mitigations (both already validated downstream):

1. **Cache the browser** so most runs skip the download entirely:

```yaml
- name: Cache Playwright browsers
  uses: actions/cache@v4
  with:
    path: ~/.cache/ms-playwright
    key: playwright-1.59.1-${{ runner.os }}
```

2. **Wrap the install in a `timeout` + retry loop** so a transient stall
   self-heals instead of consuming the whole job window:

```yaml
- name: Install Chromium for preview rendering (retry on stalled download)
  run: |
    for attempt in 1 2 3; do
      if timeout 360 npx playwright install --with-deps chromium; then
        echo "Playwright Chromium installed on attempt $attempt"
        exit 0
      fi
      echo "::warning::Playwright install attempt $attempt failed or timed out; retrying in 10s"
      sleep 10
    done
    echo "::error::Playwright Chromium install failed after 3 attempts"
    exit 1
```

Pinning the cache key to the Playwright version (`playwright-1.59.1-...`) keeps
the cache correct across upgrades.

## Context

Reported while comparing CI/CD workflows in `link-assistant/hive-mind` against
this template (link-assistant/hive-mind#1838). Happy to open a PR with the fix
if useful.

title: CI: cancel-in-progress condition is reversed, and preview-regen job lacks failure-artifact upload
body:
## Summary

Two independent CI/CD issues in this template.

### 1. Reversed `cancel-in-progress` condition

Both `example-app.yml:32` and `release.yml:42` use:

```yaml
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}
```

The `==` should be `!=`. With the current condition:

- **On `main`** the value evaluates to `true`, so a follow-up push to `main` (e.g. an automated currency/data update or a manual fix landing while a release is in flight) **cancels** the still-running release pipeline.
- **On a PR branch** the value evaluates to `false`, so every PR push starts a new run that races the previous one. Slow PR runs waste CI minutes.

The intent is the opposite: protect main from concurrent cancellation, and let PR pushes supersede older runs.

**Recommended fix:**

```yaml
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}
```

### 2. `preview-regen` job has no failure-artifact upload

`example-app.yml`'s `preview-regen` job (lines ~197-268) runs Playwright/Chromium to render preview screenshots, but has no `if: failure()` step that uploads the test-results, playwright traces, or partial screenshots. When the job fails (e.g. when a selector is wrong or the preview server hangs), the run page contains no artifacts a human can use to debug — only the raw step log.

**Recommended fix:** Add a step before/after the screenshot step:

\`\`\`yaml
- name: Upload screenshot failure artifacts
  if: failure()
  uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
  with:
    name: preview-regen-failure-\${{ github.run_id }}
    path: |
      docs/screenshots/
      web/test-results/
      web/playwright-report/
    retention-days: 7
    if-no-files-found: ignore
\`\`\`

## Where this was discovered

Found while applying template best practices to \`link-assistant/calculator\` PR #157 (https://github.com/link-assistant/calculator/pull/157). The screenshot job there hit exactly the gap described in (2) — failures were unreproducible from the run page. Both issues reported across sibling templates for consistency.

title: Add release-time hook that regenerates example-app screenshots with browser-commander
body:
## Context

`konard/vk-bot-desktop` recently shipped [PR #52](https://github.com/konard/vk-bot-desktop/pull/52) (closes [issue #51](https://github.com/konard/vk-bot-desktop/issues/51)) which adds a release-time pipeline that auto-regenerates every preview image (README + Pages site + `og:image`) using [`browser-commander`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/browser-commander) + Playwright, then commits the drift back to `main`.

While auditing CI parity I checked the four `link-foundation` AI-driven-development-pipeline-template repos and **none** ship browser automation or screenshot tooling. Full per-template survey: [`docs/case-studies/issue-51/data/templates/survey.md`](https://github.com/konard/vk-bot-desktop/blob/issue-51-60ec0489f01f/docs/case-studies/issue-51/data/templates/survey.md).

Since this template already has `.github/workflows/example-app.yml` and the richest `scripts/` ecosystem of the four, it's the natural primary host for the pattern.

## Problem

Any example app shipped from this template will accumulate stale README/site screenshots between releases. There is no automation that:

1. Boots the example app (or its built site) in a real browser headlessly.
2. Captures fresh screenshots across the locale × theme matrix.
3. Commits drift back to `main` (or surfaces it on PRs).

## Reproducible recipe

The full implementation lives at [`scripts/update-preview-images.mjs`](https://github.com/konard/vk-bot-desktop/blob/issue-51-60ec0489f01f/scripts/update-preview-images.mjs) and [the `preview-regen` job](https://github.com/konard/vk-bot-desktop/blob/issue-51-60ec0489f01f/.github/workflows/js.yml#L657) in `vk-bot-desktop`. Key building blocks worth pulling upstream:

- Static HTTP server over the renderer dist (no Electron / no devserver needed for capture).
- `browser.newContext({ locale })` to drive locale (no in-UI segmented-control toggling).
- `commander.emulateMedia({ colorScheme })` + `localStorage` to drive theme.
- `commander.page.screenshot()` because `browser-commander@0.8` exposes the raw Playwright page (no native screenshot method as of 0.10.1).
- `git status --porcelain` drift detection + `git commit -m "... [skip ci]"` push-back, so the loop is self-healing without an extra workflow.
- `PREVIEW_VERBOSE=1` to dump DOM probes (data-theme, lang, h1 contents) so CI failures are diagnosable from logs alone.

## Suggested fix

Add a `preview-regen` job to `example-app.yml` that:

1. Runs on push to `main`, on release tag pushes, and on `workflow_dispatch`.
2. Installs the existing `browser-commander` + `playwright` pin already used elsewhere.
3. Drives the example app's site through a locale × theme matrix.
4. Commits any drift to `main` with `[skip ci]`, or surfaces a workflow artifact on PRs.

Happy to send a PR if you'd like.

## Related

- konard/vk-bot-desktop#51 — original issue
- konard/vk-bot-desktop#52 — implementation PR

In the downstream start repository, command-stream returned a non-zero result from `gh api` for GitHub HTTP 422 / `already_exists`, but the script did not inspect the result code and printed a successful release message anyway. That produced a green release job even though the intended GitHub release was not created.

## Reproduction pattern

1. Ensure a release/tag already exists.
2. Run `scripts/create-github-release.mjs` for that same tag.
3. `gh api` returns a validation failure such as `already_exists`.
4. The current script can still print `Created GitHub release` because it does not validate the command result.

## Suggested fix

Use native child process execution or explicitly inspect the command-stream result code. Treat unexpected non-zero exits as failures, and treat `already_exists` as an idempotent skip only if that behavior is desired and clearly logged as a skip. Add a regression test with a fake `gh` executable that exits non-zero.

title: setup-npm.mjs should enforce npm >= 11.5.1 after fallbacks
body:
## Problem

The current template `scripts/setup-npm.mjs` documents that npm trusted publishing requires npm >= 11.5.1, but the fallback/success logic can still leave the workflow below that requirement:

- The curl fallback installs `https://registry.npmjs.org/npm/-/npm-11.4.2.tgz`, which is below the documented trusted-publishing minimum.
- If all install strategies fail, the script treats any npm major >= 11 as acceptable, even when the version is 11.0.0-11.5.0.
- The script does not re-check the final npm version against >= 11.5.1 before returning success.

npm's docs currently state that trusted publishing requires npm CLI 11.5.1 or later and Node.js 22.14.0 or higher:

https://docs.npmjs.com/trusted-publishers

## Downstream Evidence

While fixing link-foundation/lino-objects-codec#31, the JavaScript release run showed the same setup path failing to upgrade npm on GitHub Actions:

- Run: https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-objects-codec/actions/runs/25286485840
- Log evidence: bundled npm 10.9.7 failed with `Cannot find module 'promise-retry'`, then setup printed `Updated npm version: 10.9.7` and continued to publish.
- The publish later failed with npm E404/access/trusted-publisher symptoms.

## Reproduction

1. Use the current template `scripts/setup-npm.mjs`.
2. Force the standard npm install path to fail, so the curl fallback runs.
3. Observe that the fallback installs npm 11.4.2, which is below the documented trusted-publishing minimum.
4. Alternatively, make all fallback strategies fail while the current npm is any 11.x below 11.5.1; the script accepts it by major version only.

## Suggested Fix

- Parse versions numerically and enforce npm >= 11.5.1, not just major >= 11.
- Enforce Node.js >= 22.14.0 before publish setup.
- Resolve the latest npm 11.x >= 11.5.1 from registry metadata for the tarball fallback instead of pinning 11.4.2.
- After all strategies, re-run `npm --version` and fail if the result is still below 11.5.1.

This is the approach being applied downstream in link-foundation/lino-objects-codec#32.
