title: CI: add reasonable timeout-minutes to every job and per-test runner timeouts
body:
## Problem

Neither `.github/workflows/release.yml` nor `.github/workflows/links.yml` declares `timeout-minutes` on any job. Without an explicit cap, GitHub Actions falls back to its default of **six hours per job**. A flaky network call or a hung promise then blocks the AI iteration loop for hours instead of failing in minutes.

The same gap exists at the test-runner level: `npm test` runs `node --test tests/*.test.js` without `--test-timeout`, so an individual test can also hang for the full job duration before the job-level cap (if any) trips.

This defeats the "fail fast to fix flaky tests faster" property that AI-driven development depends on — the AI can only iterate as fast as CI gives it feedback.

## Evidence

```bash
# In the template's own .github/workflows/:
$ grep -rn timeout-minutes .github/workflows/
# (no matches)

$ grep -rn -- '--test-timeout\|--timeout' .github/workflows/
# (no matches)
```

## Suggested fix

Adopt the bands we landed in `link-foundation/meta-sovereign` after observing actual job p95s. Sized at roughly 5–10× the observed p95 so a real run never trips the cap, but a hung run fails in minutes:

| Band | Jobs |
|------|------|
| 5 min | `detect-changes`, `test-compilation`, `check-file-line-limits`, `version-check`, `validate-docs` |
| 10 min | `changeset-check`, `lint`, `test` (per runtime × OS), `links-checker`, `changeset-pr` |
| 15 min | `docs-build` |
| 30 min | `release`, `instant-release` |

Per-test budget (so a hung individual test fails in 30s, not at the job cap):

```json
"scripts": {
  "test": "node --test --test-timeout=30000 tests/*.test.js"
}
```

```yaml
# CI bun runner step
- run: bun test --timeout 30000
```

Deno has no global per-test timeout flag, so Deno tests stay protected only by the job-level `timeout-minutes: 10`.

## Reference implementation

Landed in https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-sovereign/pull/2 (commit 5c5fdcc). Includes:

- `.github/workflows/release.yml` + `links.yml` with `timeout-minutes` on every job, each with an inline comment recording the typical run vs. the cap so future tuning is data-driven
- `package.json` `test` script with `--test-timeout=30000`
- `docs/BEST-PRACTICES.md` §13 "Reasonable Timeouts on Every Job and Test" codifying the policy
- `README.md` testing section summarising the policy for contributors

Happy to open a PR mirroring those changes against this template if useful.

title: check-file-line-limits.sh: add 1350 warn threshold to mitigate concurrent-PR merge race
body:
## Summary

The current `scripts/check-file-line-limits.sh` enforces a hard 1500-line limit but has **no warn band**. Two PRs that each individually keep a file under 1500 can together push it over after both merge — the second PR's CI passes pre-merge, then the post-merge check on `main` is the first failure signal. Downstream Docker / Helm / Release jobs are then gated and skipped until someone notices.

This pattern has bitten downstream consumers of the template repeatedly:

- [`link-assistant/hive-mind` issue #1593](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/1593) — original concurrent-merge race.
- [`link-assistant/hive-mind` issue #1730](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/1730) — same shape, single PR adding a small block to many files near the threshold; case study at <https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1730/README.md>.

## Reproduction

1. In any repo using this template, prepare two PRs that each modify the same `.mjs` file.
2. Each PR alone leaves the file under 1500 lines (e.g. file is at 1499, PR-A adds 1 line, PR-B adds 1 line).
3. Merge PR-A. Merge PR-B. Both CI runs were green pre-merge.
4. The first CI run on `main` after PR-B fails: `ERROR: file has 1500 lines (limit: 1500)` (or above).
5. Release / build jobs are skipped because `check-file-line-limits` is a required gate.

## Suggested fix

Port the `WARN_THRESHOLD=1350` band from `link-assistant/hive-mind`'s version of the script. The 150-line gap (10% headroom) is enough to absorb typical concurrent-PR drift without being so tight that benign refactors are noisy.

Patch (functionally what hive-mind does today):

```bash
LIMIT=1500
WARN_THRESHOLD=1350
FAILURES=()
WARNINGS=()

# inside the find loop, after the >LIMIT check:
elif [ "\$line_count" -gt "\$WARN_THRESHOLD" ]; then
  WARNINGS+=(\"\$file\")
fi

# after the loop, before the failure summary:
if [ \"\${#WARNINGS[@]}\" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo \"\"
  echo \"The following files are approaching the \${LIMIT} line limit (>\${WARN_THRESHOLD} lines):\"
  printf '  %s\n' \"\${WARNINGS[@]}\"
  echo \"\"
  echo \"Consider extracting code to prevent concurrent PR merge limit violations.\"
fi
```

Hive-mind's version is here for reference: <https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/main/scripts/check-file-line-limits.sh>.

Optionally, project owners can promote warnings to errors in PRs that touch warn-band files, but the warn-only behavior is sufficient on its own — it gives reviewers a visible cue to pause and refactor before the file becomes a concurrent-merge hazard.

## Out-of-scope follow-up

While auditing the template against the same downstream incident, I noticed:

- The template's `eslint.config.js` already uses the shorthand `'max-lines': ['error', 1500]` (defaults `skipBlankLines: false, skipComments: false`), so it does **not** have the ESLint-vs-CI desync bug we just fixed in hive-mind. No change needed there.

Just adding the warn band would close the remaining gap.

title: Shields badge URL breaks when release-version contains "js-v" / "rust-v" prefix
body:
## Summary

`scripts/format-release-notes.mjs` only strips a single leading `v` before interpolating the release version into a shields.io `/badge/<label>-<message>-<color>` URL. When the caller passes a language-prefixed tag such as `js-v1.7.12` or `rust-v0.3.4`, the resulting URL contains extra unescaped `-` separators and shields.io returns the SVG `404: badge not found`.

This template works correctly for consumers that use a plain `v<version>` tag, but any downstream repo that multiplexes JS and Rust releases under `js-v<version>` / `rust-v<version>` tags hits the bug. For concrete evidence see [link-assistant/web-capture#98](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture/issues/98) and the [fix PR link-assistant/web-capture#99](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture/pull/99).

## Reproduction

```bash
curl -sS 'https://img.shields.io/badge/npm-js-v1.7.12-blue.svg' | head -c 200
```

Returns an SVG whose `aria-label="404: badge not found"`. The working form is:

```bash
curl -sS 'https://img.shields.io/badge/npm-1.7.12-blue.svg' | head -c 200
```

Which returns `aria-label="npm: 1.7.12"`.

## Offending line

`scripts/format-release-notes.mjs`:

```js
const versionWithoutV = version.replace(/^v/, '');
```

`version.replace(/^v/, '')` strips a leading single `v`. Given `js-v1.7.12`, `versionWithoutV` stays `js-v1.7.12`, and the next line interpolates it into a URL with four `-`-separated fields instead of the three that shields.io parses.

## Suggested fix

Pick one of the following. All are backward-compatible with consumers that pass a plain `v<version>`:

1. **Normalize the passed string** (what link-assistant/web-capture#99 ships):

   ```js
   const versionWithoutV = version
     .replace(/^[a-z]+-/i, '')   // drop "js-", "rust-", etc.
     .replace(/^v/i, '');        // drop leading "v"
   ```

2. **Use the dynamic shields endpoint** so the badge reads the current npm version directly and does not depend on the tag string:

   ```js
   const npmBadge = `[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/${PACKAGE_NAME}?label=npm&color=blue)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/${PACKAGE_NAME})`;
   ```

3. **Encourage callers to pass the clean numeric version** from `steps.publish.outputs.published_version` rather than the tag. `scripts/format-github-release.mjs` currently passes the full tag - it could strip the prefix at the call site instead.

## Workaround for affected downstreams

Until upstream fixes this, downstream consumers can override the version normalization as in link-assistant/web-capture@7ee8fe6 and optionally run a one-shot repair like [link-assistant/web-capture's fix-existing-release-badges.mjs](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture/blob/main/scripts/fix-existing-release-badges.mjs) against already-published releases.

## Related

- Rust pipeline template sidesteps the issue because it uses `/crates/v/<name>` (dynamic) rather than `/badge/...` (static).
- shields.io /badge syntax reference: https://shields.io/badges/static-badge

feat: add self-healing release pipeline for unreleased changes
body:
## Summary

Fixes #36

- Add `scripts/check-release-needed.mjs` — checks npm registry to detect unpublished versions, enabling releases even without changesets (analogous to Rust template's `check-release-needed.rs`)
- Update `release.yml` — integrate the new script as a self-healing fallback path in the release job
- Add case study documentation in `docs/case-studies/issue-36/`

## Problem

The release job was gated entirely on the presence of changeset files. If a PR merged without a changeset, the release job silently did nothing, leaving merged fixes unreleased indefinitely. This was documented in [link-assistant/web-capture#56](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture/issues/56).

## Solution

The new `check-release-needed.mjs` script runs after `check-changesets` and checks the npm registry:

1. **Changesets exist** → normal flow (`should_release=true`, `skip_bump=false`)
2. **No changesets, version not on npm** → self-healing (`should_release=true`, `skip_bump=true`) — publishes the current version directly
3. **No changesets, version already on npm** → no action needed (`should_release=false`)

The publish step in `release.yml` now has a third condition for the self-healing path:

```yaml
if: >-
  steps.version.outputs.version_committed == 'true' ||
  steps.version.outputs.already_released == 'true' ||
  (steps.check_release.outputs.should_release == 'true' && steps.check_release.outputs.skip_bump == 'true')
```

title: Release job silently skips when PRs merge without changesets — unreleased fixes accumulate
body:
## Summary

The `release` job in `release.yml` gates publishing entirely on the presence of changeset files in `.changeset/`. If a PR merges to main without a changeset (which can happen for bugfixes, CI changes, dependency bumps, etc.), the release job silently does nothing, leaving merged fixes unreleased indefinitely.

## Root Cause

In `release.yml` lines 390-407:

```yaml
- name: Check for changesets
  id: check_changesets
  run: node scripts/check-changesets.mjs

- name: Version packages and commit to main
  if: steps.check_changesets.outputs.has_changesets == 'true'
  ...

- name: Publish to npm
  if: steps.version.outputs.version_committed == 'true' || steps.version.outputs.already_released == 'true'
```

The entire release flow is gated on `has_changesets == 'true'`. No changesets → no version step → no publish → no release.

## Impact

Users running `npm install <package>` get a stale version that doesn't include merged fixes. This is the exact issue documented in link-assistant/web-capture#56.

## Comparison with Rust Template

The [rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template](https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template) already handles this correctly via `check-release-needed.rs`, which:
1. Checks crates.io (not just local state) to determine if the current version is published
2. If the version isn't published, proceeds with release even without fragments
3. Acts as a self-healing mechanism for accumulated unreleased changes

## Suggested Fix

Add a `check-release-needed.mjs` script (analogous to the Rust template's `check-release-needed.rs`) that:

1. Checks npm registry to see if the current `package.json` version is published
2. If not published → signal release needed (no changeset required)
3. If published → check for unreleased commits since the last release tag that touch publishable paths
4. If unreleased publishable changes found → auto-bump patch version and release

This ensures the pipeline is **self-healing**: any push to main that includes unreleased code will trigger a release, regardless of whether a changeset was included.

## Reproduction

1. Create a PR that changes `src/` files without adding a `.changeset/*.md` file
2. Merge the PR to main
3. Observe that the release job in CI runs but publishes nothing
4. `npm view <package> version` still shows the old version

## Related

- link-assistant/web-capture#56 — same issue in a downstream project using this template
- link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template — already has the fix via `check-release-needed.rs`

title: fix: npm upgrade fallbacks and Node.js 24.x upgrade for CI/CD
body:
## Summary

Fixes #33 — `setup-npm.mjs` fails on GitHub Actions when Node.js 22.22.2 ships with broken npm 10.9.7 (missing `promise-retry` module).

### Changes

- **Upgrade Node.js 20.x → 24.x** in all workflow files (6 locations in `release.yml`). Node.js 24.x (Active LTS) ships with npm 11.x which doesn't have the `promise-retry` bug.
- **Add 4-strategy fallback chain** to `setup-npm.mjs`:
  1. Standard `npm install -g npm@11`
  2. Curl tarball download (bypasses broken npm entirely)
  3. npx-based install
  4. Corepack as last resort
- **Update GitHub Actions** to latest major versions:
  - `actions/checkout`: v4 → v6
  - `actions/setup-node`: v4 → v6
  - `peter-evans/create-pull-request`: v7 → v8
- **Fix test command** for Node.js 24 compatibility: `node --test tests/` → `node --test tests/*.test.js` (Node 24 changed how directory arguments are handled)
- **Exit with error code 1** when all npm upgrade strategies fail (instead of silently continuing)

title: Workflow concurrency: cancel-in-progress on main can cancel active releases
body:
## Problem

The `release.yml` workflow uses:

```yaml
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}
```

This cancels in-progress runs **on main** — which is exactly where releases happen. When the version-and-commit step pushes a new commit to main, it triggers a new workflow run that may cancel the currently running release before publish completes.

## Expected Behavior

- **Main branch:** Never cancel active runs (releases should complete)
- **PR branches:** Cancel stale runs when new commits are pushed

## Suggested Fix

Invert the condition:

```yaml
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}
```

## Reference

See [link-assistant/web-capture#55](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture/pull/55) for the same fix applied in a downstream project.

title: setup-npm.mjs: npm upgrade fails on GitHub Actions with Node.js 22.22.2 (broken npm 10.9.7)
body:
## Problem

`setup-npm.mjs` fails to upgrade npm on GitHub Actions runners with Node.js 22.22.2. The bundled npm 10.9.7 is missing the `promise-retry` module, causing `npm install -g npm@latest` to fail with `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`.

This means `npm publish --provenance` (OIDC trusted publishing) fails because it requires npm >= 11.5.1.

## Reproduction

Run a GitHub Actions workflow on `ubuntu-latest` with `node-version: '22.x'` that calls `node scripts/setup-npm.mjs`:

```
npm error code MODULE_NOT_FOUND
npm error Cannot find module 'promise-retry'
npm error Require stack:
npm error - /opt/hostedtoolcache/node/22.22.2/x64/lib/node_modules/npm/node_modules/@npmcli/arborist/lib/arborist/rebuild.js
```

## Upstream Issues

- [actions/runner-images#13883](https://github.com/actions/runner-images/issues/13883)
- [nodejs/node#62430](https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/62430)
- [npm/cli#9151](https://github.com/npm/cli/issues/9151)

## Workaround

Download npm tarball directly via `curl`, bypassing the broken npm entirely:

```javascript
const nodeDir = run("dirname $(dirname $(which node))");
const globalNpmDir = `${nodeDir}/lib/node_modules/npm`;
run(
  `curl -sL https://registry.npmjs.org/npm/-/npm-11.4.2.tgz | ` +
  `tar xz -C /tmp && ` +
  `rm -rf "${globalNpmDir}" && ` +
  `mv /tmp/package "${globalNpmDir}"`
);
```

## Suggested Fix

Add the curl-based tarball download as a fallback strategy in `setup-npm.mjs` (between the standard `npm install -g` and the npx/corepack fallbacks). Also exit with error code 1 when all strategies fail instead of silently continuing with broken npm.

See [link-assistant/web-capture#55](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture/pull/55) for a reference implementation.

title: fix: use per-commit diff instead of full-PR diff for change detection
body:
## Summary

- **Per-commit diff instead of full-PR diff**: detect-code-changes.mjs now uses `HEAD^2^..HEAD^2` for PR merge commits (GitHub Actions synthetic merge) to evaluate only what the latest push changed, not the entire PR
- **Remove unused env vars**: `GITHUB_BASE_SHA`/`GITHUB_HEAD_SHA` removed from workflow since merge commit detection is self-contained via `git cat-file`
- **Case study**: Root cause analysis with timeline, evidence from web-capture PR #49, and verification plan

Fixes #31

## Root Cause

Two separate issues were causing unnecessary CI runs:

1. **`GITHUB_BASE_SHA...GITHUB_HEAD_SHA` comparison** — the script compared the PR base against the PR head, giving the full PR diff (all files changed across the entire PR)

2. **GitHub Actions synthetic merge commit** — even `HEAD^..HEAD` gives the full PR diff, because GitHub creates a merge commit where `HEAD^` is the base branch

**Evidence**: In [web-capture PR #49](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture/pull/49), commit `0e9b6e8c` only modified `.gitkeep` but triggered all 8 CI jobs because the PR as a whole contained code changes.

## Solution

Detect the synthetic merge commit and use `HEAD^2^..HEAD^2` (per-commit diff of the actual PR head):

```javascript
function isMergeCommit() {
  const parentCount = exec('git cat-file -p HEAD')
    .split('\n')
    .filter((line) => line.startsWith('parent ')).length;
  return parentCount > 1;
}
```

- `HEAD` = synthetic merge commit
- `HEAD^` = base branch (first parent)
- `HEAD^2` = actual PR head commit (second parent)
- `HEAD^2^` = PR head commit's parent

For push events, the regular `HEAD^..HEAD` is used.

This follows the same approach implemented and verified in [web-capture PR #51](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture/pull/51).

## Files Changed

| `scripts/detect-code-changes.mjs` | Replace full-PR diff with per-commit diff via merge commit detection |

body:
## Summary

This PR incorporates best CI/CD practices from the [hive-mind repository](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind), specifically addressing the critical issue of **stale merge preview** in GitHub Actions.

### Key Changes

1. **Fresh Merge Simulation**: Added to both `lint` and `test` jobs in the CI workflow
   - Fetches the latest base branch when running PR checks
   - Merges it to simulate the actual merge result
   - Prevents stale merge preview issues where PRs pass CI but fail after merge

2. **Case Study Documentation**: Comprehensive analysis in `docs/case-studies/issue-23/`
   - Root cause analysis of GitHub's merge preview architecture
   - Timeline of events from hive-mind issue #1141
   - Online research on best practices
   - Raw data from referenced PRs for future reference

3. **Configuration Updates**:
   - Add ignore patterns for case study data files in ESLint and Prettier
   - Update lint-staged to suppress warnings for ignored files

### The Problem Being Solved

When a PR triggers a GitHub Actions workflow, GitHub creates a synthetic merge commit at `refs/pull/{number}/merge`. This is a **snapshot** that does NOT automatically update when the base branch changes. This leads to:

```
Day 1: PR opened -> CI passes (validates against snapshot)
[Time passes - other PRs merge to main]
Day N: PR merged -> Main CI fails (actual merge differs from snapshot)
```

### The Solution

The fresh merge simulation step ensures PR CI validates the **actual** merge result:

```yaml
- name: Simulate fresh merge with base branch (PR only)
  if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
  run: |
    git fetch origin "$BASE_REF"
    BEHIND_COUNT=$(git rev-list --count HEAD..origin/$BASE_REF)
    if [ "$BEHIND_COUNT" -gt 0 ]; then
      git merge origin/$BASE_REF --no-edit || exit 1
    fi
```

## Summary

This PR improves the changeset CI/CD robustness by implementing solutions from hive-mind PR #961. The key improvements:

- **PR Validation**: Only validates changesets **added by the current PR**, not pre-existing ones from other merged PRs
- **Release-time Merging**: Automatically merges multiple pending changesets with highest version bump type
- **Documentation**: Comprehensive case study and README updates

### Changes Made

1. **Update `validate-changeset.mjs`**
   - Uses git diff to compare PR head vs base SHA
   - Only validates changesets ADDED by the current PR (not pre-existing ones)
   - Falls back to checking all changesets for local development
   - Refactored to reduce complexity by extracting helper functions

2. **Add `merge-changesets.mjs`**
   - Combines multiple pending changesets into a single merged changeset during release
   - Uses the highest version bump type (major > minor > patch)
   - Preserves all descriptions in chronological order (by file modification time)
   - Cleans up individual changeset files after merging

3. **Update `release.yml` workflow**
   - Pass `GITHUB_BASE_SHA` and `GITHUB_HEAD_SHA` environment variables to validation script
   - Add step to merge multiple changesets before running `changeset version`

4. **Add comprehensive tests**
   - Tests for both `validate-changeset.mjs` and `merge-changesets.mjs`
   - Tests for bump type priority, chronological ordering, edge cases

5. **Add case study documentation**
   - Timeline of events leading to the issue
   - Root cause analysis
   - Solutions and industry best practices
   - Reference data from hive-mind PR #961

### How It Works

**During PR validation:**
```
Before: Check all .changeset/*.md files → Fail if >1 exists
After:  Check only files ADDED in this PR → Fail if >1 was added
```

**During release:**
```
Before: changeset version → (fail if multiple changesets)
After:  merge-changesets.mjs → changeset version → (always single changeset)
```

### Benefits

1. **No more false failures** - PRs won't fail just because other PRs merged first
2. **Preserved sequence** - Changesets are merged chronologically
3. **Correct version bumps** - Major changes won't be downgraded to patch
4. **Backward compatible** - Local development still works without git context

### Configuration Details

All rules are configured at the **'warn'** level (not 'error') to:
- Provide helpful feedback to developers
- Highlight potential refactoring opportunities
- Avoid blocking development or causing CI failures
- Encourage but not enforce code quality improvements

- The 1500 limit is the total physical line count of the file
